source_type: read-only source audit; no automatic capacity implementation

sources.source_reading: Finite logical fields or existing IPC declarations. Ordinary request capacity still comes from RecordsResources; not a physical grant.
Actual process-local membership and sum of storage grants checked against an existing Core; compute remains globally checked. Does not discover physical bytes.
Allocates lifetime payload envelopes including siblings; actual row charges last through release. Does not cover whole process RSS.
Uses one existing service Core and partitions a Job grant across dependent flows. This is a different owner from the private records query Core.
Currently creates its own MethodBudgetPool from the query capacity. No supplied service Job capability is used here.
Own finite request, input, result and control declarations. Their defaults are not observed available memory.

existing_components_to_reuse: SessionEngine and JobRegistry membership and storage checks
Existing IPC input, result, command and control reservations
missing: A service/deployment owner that actually controls an exclusive finite byte assignment for all concurrent records owners.
Wire that assignment into the existing Core and Method grants and child IPC declarations without giving each simultaneous copy the entire assignment.
Account simultaneous prepared input, serialized RPC/IPC copies, unconsumed results and unknown work until their existing owners release them.
Reject unavailable or foreign grant evidence before starting workers; test sibling queries, model-owner changes, slow consumers and partial cleanup.
not_grant_sources: Shared cgroup limit or observed headroom
RSS watchdog or incomplete kernel memory observation
vLLM scheduler settings, model context or a requested R
A user-created copy of a visible JobHandle label
qualification: The source audit identifies reusable owners and missing wiring. It neither assigns hardware capacity nor changes current request defaults.

followup.source_type: Engineering design from current source; no physical allocation source is implemented

implemented.scope: Convert already-assigned input/result/Method payload bytes to an existing complete logical budget. Does not acquire an allocation.
Direct owner and factory use the same IPC default resolver; explicit IPC is preserved.

actual_call_chain: Deployment/service owner supplies assigned storage; authoritative source still missing.
records_capacity converts assigned bytes without probing RAM.
records_profile resolves one set of Core and IPC values before actor construction.
Existing actor ready binds actual model identity; Core and Method retain their current result and unknown rules.
missing_owner_facts: The service or deployment allocator actually controls the allocation, rather than merely observes shared headroom.
The allocation is claimed by the actual owner once; its service, model instance and generation can be verified.
Concurrent model owners cannot each spend the same whole allocation.
Allocated scope explicitly includes simultaneous input/state/result copies, or states what is caller-owned and separately accounted.
followup.existing_service_reuse: PG JobRegistry storage shares are real only on that same shared Core. The private records owners currently build different Cores/backends; copying a Job label or creating an unused Core cannot establish global compute or storage ownership for them.
lifetime_checks: Claim before workers or model construction.
Bind successful ready to the same actual owner/model; a path or requested spec alone is insufficient.
Uncertain startup and unknown computation keep their allocation until the existing producer evidence is confirmed.
Unconsumed results and local borrowing keep their respective allocations; model close alone is not result-consumption acknowledgement.
Resident queries may reuse the same claimed instance; a replacement owner needs a distinct allocation or proved complete release.

next_files.action: Consume a supplied verified allocation in pure preflight, rather than infer it from defaults.
Obtain and claim it from the service/deployment owner before Ray and carry the same allocation through the session.
Bind the allocation to the actual ready model and preserve uncertain startup evidence.
Retain existing ACK and producer proof; release allocation only after the matching producer and consumer holdings settle.

required_CPU_counterexamples: Double claim and concurrent owner spending
Partial startup with uncertain child ownership
Same-instance query reuse and final release
